properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean Carboniferous sedimentary strata (sandstone, siltstone, and mudstone) interspersed with igneous dolerite intrusions along the Water of Leith valley. Structural masonry composed of local Craigleith and Hailes pale buff-to-grey quartz-rich sandstone. Bedding laid with non-hydraulic to weakly hydraulic slaked lime mortar. Sloping alluvial gravels and glacial till ensure rapid urban runoff.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Urban woodland margin featuring *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Late-November phenology exhibits full autumn defoliation, revealing bare, intricate branch architectures with sparse residual brown leaf clusters and ground-level leaf litter along kerbs.

properties.architectural_summary:
Left: Victorian residential tenement block; planar vertical rectification, three-storey massing with projecting canted multi-tier bay windows, molded stone cornices, and timber 2-over-2 sash-and-case fenestration grids.
Center: Gothic Revival ecclesiastical structure; rectangular nave with buttressed bays, pointed-arch fenestration, and a prominent square bell tower topped with crenellated parapets and corner pinnacles.
Surrounds: Low dressed-sandstone boundary retaining walls along the road corridor.
